# Harvard Investment Group

> Harvard Investment Group, founded in 1995 by Greg Cullen, invests in value-added real estate and early stage businesses and develops luxury residential real estate in Southern California. Office: 6060 W Manchester Ave, Suite 304, Los Angeles, CA 90045. Phone (310) 702-5252. Email greg@harvardinvestmentgroup.com.

## About Greg Cullen
Greg Cullen is the founder of Harvard Investment Group. Harvard Investment Group was founded in 1995 to make direct investments and provide services to early stage corporations and real estate ventures. Since its inception, Harvard Investment Group and Mr. Cullen have been the lead investor and an active partner in dozens of transactions with a combined value approaching a billion dollars. Investments have been made in companies involved in media, artificial intelligence, pharmaceutical, finance, medical devices, fast food, energy, real estate, entertainment, apparel and the like.

Mr. Cullen has a strong finance/banking background having spent time working for both Citibank and ING Capital Corporation prior to forming Harvard Investment Group. He is actively involved in all aspects of deal creation, finance, strategy, and partner relations. With a focus on executive oversight on the company’s development projects and corporate investments, he is an accomplished and results-oriented professional with over thirty years’ experience in private equity and real estate development.

Mr. Cullen graduated with a Master’s Degree in Business Administration from the Harvard Business School in 1989. His emphasis there was on real estate. He graduated with honors from Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology in 1985, where he received a Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering. Mr. Cullen is a highly sought after speaker and considered to be an expert in the fields of real estate, finance, negotiations and value creation. Mr. Cullen is the former President of the Harvard Real Estate Alumni Organization and sits on various corporate boards.

## Investments
Harvard Investment Group makes investments in both value-added real estate opportunities and early stage businesses. The Company directly, or through its affiliated organizations, invests capital in value-added real estate projects and early stage businesses that are in need of capital and/or management expertise.

The Company typically invests anywhere from the mid-five figures to seven figures, depending on the transaction. The goal of the Company is to work with its investment target companies to build a solid management team, a firm financial foundation and a strategy that leads to a profitable exit.

The Company, and its team of professionals, has expertise in deal structuring, valuation, financial engineering, corporate strategy and value creation. Its Principal often provides direction and corporate support at the board level, but also has assisted companies – on an interim basis – by acting in an executive capacity and in operational roles.

## Developments
Harvard Investment Group is a vertically integrated real estate development company. The Company directly, or through its affiliated entities, acquires real estate assets with value added potential. The Company specializes in purchasing land with unrealized development potential and underperforming real estate assets. With its experienced team of professionals, the Company undertakes the process of transforming its real estate holdings into for sale product or assets held for cash flow.

The Company has expertise in all aspects of the development process including acquisition, deal structuring, finance, architectural design, entitlements, construction – ranging from home remodeling to full scale land subdivision and project development, and real estate sales. The principal of the Company is both a licensed contractor and licensed real estate broker in the State of California.

### Corona Del Mar
This exclusive development consists of two luxury estates built on the sands of Newport Harbor. Each home has approximately 10,000 square feet of livable area and has all the amenities that you can dream of. From your new home, you can dine at the water’s edge, step on to your own sandy beach and take a swim, or stroll down your private dock and climb aboard your 85-foot yacht.

### Bayside 2201 (Sold for $24,500,000)
This modern masterpiece was designed by Brandon Architects and Brooke Wagner Design. It features five bedrooms and nine bathrooms on four levels of luxurious living. Other amenities include an incomparable master suite, stunning views, a rooftop deck with views of the world, wine room, elevator, outdoor fire pit, pool, jacuzzi and a 6-car garage.

### Bayside 2209 (Sold for $23,000,000)
This charming Cape Cod estate was also designed by Brandon Architects and Brooke Wagner Design. It features six bedrooms and eight bathrooms on four levels of luxurious living with soaring ceilings and open floor plans. Other amenities include a spacious master suite with a fireplace lounge, stunning views, a rooftop deck with views of the world, wine room, elevator, outdoor fire pit and water feature, pool, jacuzzi and a 6-car garage.

### Hollywood Hills
This infamous modern masterpiece was designed by Tag Front, and is built into the side of the Hollywood Hills with views of the Pacific Ocean and unending city views. The home features close to 6,000 square feet of seamlessly designed interior living space with immense scale and openness. Comprised of 4 bedroom suites, multiple guest baths, cook’s kitchen, sculptural fireplace, pool lounge and infinity edge pool and spa, this home is crafted for entertainment.

### Hermosa Beach
This four-unit development, consisting of both coastal plantation and modern style homes, is perched on the hills of Hermosa Beach with breathtaking views of the ocean and Catalina Island. Each home has almost 3,300 square feet of interior living space, along with an oversized living room balcony and a roof deck. The homes feature 4 bedrooms, 5 bathrooms, high ceilings, an open floor plan, and a state of the art kitchen.

### Redondo Beach
This modern, three-unit, townhome development is nestled in the hills of Redondo Beach. Each home has unimpeded views of the ocean and Catalina Island. Each home has approximately 2,700 square feet of interior living space, along with a living room balcony and a roof deck. The homes feature 4 bedrooms, 4 bathrooms, high ceilings, open floor plan, and a state of the art kitchen.

## Philanthropic: Hope for the Hurting
In 2015, Mr. Cullen formed Hope for the Hurting as a 501(c)(3) charitable organization with a mission to assist the less fortunate among us and provide a foundation for people to improve their lives. With the help of several generous donors, Hope for the Hurting, which started with a single location in Los Angeles, has expanded to multiple locations in both California and Indiana.

The charity now has four facilities that serve men and women who struggle with mental illness and/or drug and alcohol addiction. These facilities provide housing, food and varying levels of counseling and medical services to assist the clients. In addition, the charity through its Strike Out Against Drugs program, actively speaks to children in school settings throughout the Los Angeles area. The goal is to persuade children to avoid a pathway which leads to the experimentation and use of alcohol and drugs. SOAD has touched the lives of tens of thousands of children and adults in the Los Angeles area and has received numerous awards.

### Beacon of Hope, Los Angeles (https://www.beaconofhope.la/)
The Beacon of Hope facility located just west of downtown Los Angeles was the first major undertaking for the charity. This beautiful Victorian residence has been home to thousands of men since opening in 2013. It is a refuge for men seeking help for addiction and/or mental health challenges. Over the years, it has developed a reputation as being one of the best run facilities of its type in the Los Angeles area.

### Wabash Recovery, Kokomo
What once was an unused church building in Kokomo, Indiana, has been transformed into a home for men seeking help for drug and alcohol dependency issues. It was built to help meet the needs of this vastly underserved population.

### Oasis Recovery, Tipton
The charity received a donation from an extremely generous couple, who were like-minded in their desire to help people with substance abuse issues. This property consists of two homes located on five acres in the beautiful countryside of rural Indiana. The charity is in the process of obtaining licenses and approvals to operate a residential facility at this location that provides full time care for people in need.

### Strike Out Against Drugs (https://www.strikeoutagainstdrugs.com/)
SOAD is led by individuals who are dedicated to keeping children from a life of drug and alcohol abuse. Through real-life testimonies and outreach programs, SOAD is sending a positive message to our children before they become involved in destructive types of behaviors, all of which can lead to violence or illegal activities. Through the sharing of personal experiences of how this type of lifestyle has destroyed countless lives, SOAD’s real-life messages cannot be matched by any text book or statistic. We are real people telling our stories. To date, this message has been communicated to thousands upon thousands of children in Southern California.

## FAQ
**What is Harvard Investment Group?**
Harvard Investment Group is a multi-dimensional organization, founded in 1995 by Greg Cullen, that has been actively investing in and developing real estate for over three decades, along with its affiliated companies. It also makes direct investments in early stage businesses.

**Who leads Harvard Investment Group?**
Greg Cullen, the founder. He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School (1989) and a mechanical engineering degree from Rose-Hulman (1985), worked at Citibank and ING Capital before founding the company, and is a licensed contractor and real estate broker in California.

**Where is Harvard Investment Group based?**
The office is at 6060 W Manchester Ave, Suite 304, Los Angeles, CA 90045. Development projects have been in Corona del Mar (Newport Beach), the Hollywood Hills, Hermosa Beach and Redondo Beach.

**What does Harvard Investment Group invest in?**
Value-added real estate opportunities and early stage businesses that need capital and/or management expertise. Past investments span media, artificial intelligence, pharmaceutical, finance, medical devices, fast food, energy, real estate, entertainment and apparel.

**How much does Harvard Investment Group typically invest?**
Anywhere from the mid-five figures to seven figures, depending on the transaction. The goal is to help build a solid management team, a firm financial foundation and a strategy that leads to a profitable exit.

**Does Harvard Investment Group take an active role in its investments?**
Yes. Its principal often provides direction and corporate support at the board level, and has also assisted companies on an interim basis in executive and operational roles.

**What kind of real estate does Harvard Investment Group develop?**
It is a vertically integrated developer that buys land with unrealized development potential and underperforming real estate assets, then transforms them into for-sale product or assets held for cash flow. Work has ranged from home remodeling to full-scale land subdivision and project development.

**What is the Corona del Mar development?**
Two luxury estates built on the sands of Newport Harbor, each with roughly 10,000 square feet of livable area, a private beach and a private dock. 2201 Bayside Drive sold for $24,500,000 and 2209 Bayside Drive sold for $23,000,000.

**Was a Harvard Investment Group project featured on Netflix?**
Yes. The Corona del Mar project appears in Selling the OC, Season 3, on Netflix.

**Who designed 2201 Bayside Drive?**
Brandon Architects, with interiors by Brooke Wagner Design. The home has five bedrooms and nine bathrooms on four levels, a rooftop deck, wine room, elevator, outdoor fire pit, pool, jacuzzi and a 6-car garage.

**What is Hope for the Hurting?**
A 501(c)(3) charitable organization Mr. Cullen formed in 2015 to assist the less fortunate and provide a foundation for people to improve their lives. It operates four facilities in California and Indiana for men and women facing mental illness and/or addiction, and runs the Strike Out Against Drugs school program.

**I’m a founder looking for funding. Is Harvard Investment Group a fit?**
Possibly. Harvard Investment Group invests in early stage businesses that need capital and/or management expertise, typically from the mid-five figures to seven figures, depending on the transaction. It has invested in media, artificial intelligence, pharmaceuticals, finance, medical devices, fast food, energy, real estate, entertainment and apparel. Every opportunity is reviewed individually by Greg Cullen.

**How do I pitch my company?**
Send a short summary to Greg Cullen’s office through the contact page: the company name and what it does, the stage it is at, how much capital it is raising and what for, and the founder’s name, email and phone number. Every decision follows a review; nothing is promised in advance.

**Can Harvard Investment Group help beyond money?**
Yes. Its principal often supports companies at the board level and has stepped into interim executive and operational roles. The team brings expertise in deal structuring, valuation, financial engineering, corporate strategy and value creation.

**Do you buy land or underperforming properties?**
That is the company’s specialty: land with unrealized development potential and underperforming real estate assets, which it transforms into homes for sale or assets held for cash flow. A seller or broker with a property should share the address and details with Greg Cullen’s office through the contact page.

**Does Harvard Investment Group take on development partners?**
It works with partners on land, entitlements, construction and sales, and handles every part of the process itself: acquisition, deal structuring, finance, architectural design, entitlements, construction and real estate sales. Anyone with a site, a project or a partnership idea should send a short description through the contact page.

**Are any of your homes for sale right now?**
The homes on this site are completed projects, and the two Corona del Mar estates have sold. For current or upcoming opportunities, ask Greg Cullen’s office through the contact page.

**How do I donate to Hope for the Hurting, and is it tax deductible?**
Donate through Hope for the Hurting’s own website, hopefth.org. Hope for the Hurting is a 501(c)(3) charitable organization and all donations are tax deductible; confirm the details with your own tax advisor. Donations support its four facilities for men and women facing mental illness and/or addiction, and the Strike Out Against Drugs program in Los Angeles schools.

**Can I donate property or other assets?**
The charity has received property before: Oasis Recovery in Indiana was a donation from a generous couple. Anyone considering a gift like that should speak with Greg Cullen’s office.

**Is Greg Cullen available to speak at events?**
Yes. Mr. Cullen is a highly sought-after speaker and is considered an expert in real estate, finance, negotiations and value creation. Send speaking requests to his office through the contact page.

**How can I contact Harvard Investment Group?**
Email greg@harvardinvestmentgroup.com, call (310) 702-5252, or send a message through the contact page. The office is at 6060 W Manchester Ave, Suite 304, Los Angeles, CA 90045.
